artworks.title: Capaneus (Illustrations to Dante's Inferno)
artworks.description: Blake's watercolour for Inferno XIV sets Capaneus under the rain of fire — Dante's blasphemer still scorning Jove, the Theban who climbed the walls and was struck by lightning.

artworks.title: Head of Capaneus the Blasphemer
artworks.description: Girodet's study isolates the defiant face Dante memorialized — Capaneus as the type of the blasphemer who will not bend even in Hell's burning sand.

artworks.title: Capaneus Struck by Zeus (Etruscan urn relief)
artworks.description: An Etruscan ash-urn relief (Würzburg) shows Capaneus blasted from the Theban wall — Zeus' bolt answering the hero who said even the gods could not stop him.

popCulture.title: Inferno
popCulture.creator: Dante Alighieri
popCulture.description: Dante seats Capaneus among the blasphemers in the seventh circle — still cursing Jove under the flakes of fire, the Seven Against Thebes rewritten as eternal defiance.

popCulture.title: Seven Against Thebes
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus makes Capaneus the loudest of the seven: the giant-hearted attacker whose ladder and blasphemy Zeus answers with lightning at the gate.

popCulture.title: Capaneus
popCulture.description: Son of Hipponous, one of the Seven Against Thebes — struck by Zeus for boasting that not even the gods could keep him from the wall.
